title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a normal, irreducible variety of finite type over a field k of characteristic 0. M(X) is Grothendieck's category of motives over X. v and w are two 'archimedean places', i.e. complex points coming from embeddings of k (or of k(X)) into C. Each gives an integral Betti fibre functor xi^Z_v, xi^Z_w on M(X).

Two questions are posed:
(a) Are xi^Z_v and xi^Z_w isomorphic as tensor functors?
(b) Weaker: for every finitely generated tensor ('multiplicative') subcategory M_alpha(X) of M(X), are the restrictions to M_alpha(X) isomorphic?

Preliminary reduction. Replace k by its algebraic closure k' in k(X). Because X is normal, k' is contained in O(X), so X is a k'-variety. Now k' is algebraically closed in k(X), hence X is geometrically irreducible. Let k_0 (also called E) be the algebraic closure of Q in k.

Claim 1). If v and w agree on k_0, then xi_v|M_alpha is isomorphic to xi_w|M_alpha for every alpha.
Proof sketch:
- Spread out. X and the finitely many motives generating M_alpha are defined over a finitely generated k_0-subalgebra A_0 of k, giving X_0 -> Spec A_0.
- Shrink Spec A_0 (marginal note [x]) so that X_0 -> Spec A_0 is smooth with geometrically connected fibres and Spec A_0 is smooth and connected over k_0. Then X_0 is smooth and geometrically connected over k_0.
- The two complex points then lie in the single connected complex manifold X_0 tensor_{k_0,sigma} C, where sigma is the common restriction to k_0.
- The realisations of motives in M_alpha are local systems on it. A path between the two points (the transcendental fundamental groupoid) gives a tensor isomorphism of fibre functors.
This isomorphism depends on the model, so it is only obtained alpha by alpha; a global isomorphism on all of M(X) would require compatible choices of paths across the inverse system.

Claim b) is left fragmentary. If v and w agree on k one has more (equality); if they differ on k_0 the functors are in general not isomorphic, xi_v != xi_w (cf. Galois action, Serre's conjugate varieties).

This serves the 'Galois theory of motives' programme: the dependence of the motivic Galois groupoid / Betti fibre functors on the choice of complex embedding. Only the restriction of the embedding to k_0 = Q-bar ∩ k matters, up to isomorphism on finitely generated pieces.
errors: Normal + irreducible over k does not by itself make k algebraically closed in k(X). Grothendieck handles this by replacing k by its algebraic closure in k(X), which is legitimate only because X is normal, as he notes.
An embedding of k into C does not by itself give a complex point of X. The 'places of X' must be read as complex points (e.g. embeddings of k(X)), and this is left implicit.
Part (a) is not settled. Only the alpha-by-alpha isomorphism is proved. Passing to all of M(X) involves a lim^1-type compatibility problem for the path choices, which is not addressed.
Part b) is left incomplete and partly crossed out.
The parenthetical '(p.ex. k_0 alg. fini sur k)' seems confused, probably meant 'fini sur Q'.

ideas.what: Spreading out a variety and finitely many motives to a smooth model with geometrically connected fibres over a smooth connected base finitely generated over Q-bar∩k.
ideas.modern_name: spreading out / reduction to finitely generated base

ideas.what: Betti fibre functors at complex points lying over the same embedding of Q-bar∩k are isomorphic, via paths in a connected complex family (topological fundamental groupoid). Only the restriction of the embedding to the algebraic closure of Q matters.
ideas.modern_name: independence of Betti realisation (up to isomorphism) from the embedding beyond Q-bar; deformation invariance; cf. Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles, Ayoub's/Nori's motivic Galois groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, 1982); Serre for the converse failure over number fields (1964)

ideas.what: Isomorphism only on each finitely generated tensor subcategory M_alpha, not a priori on all of M(X).
ideas.modern_name: pro-systems of fibre functors / torsor of isomorphisms over the motivic Galois group, lim^1 obstruction

missed.claim: Whether two integral Betti fibre functors on motives over X, for complex points agreeing on Q-bar∩k, are isomorphic globally on M(X), rather than only on each finitely generated subcategory. This is a compatibility / lim^1 question across models, explicitly raised but unresolved.
missed.quote: Ou du moins, est-il vrai que pour tout système mult. de f.f. de M(X), les restrictions de ces foncteurs à M_alpha(X) soient isomorphes ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It bears on whether the integral motivic Galois torsor between embeddings is trivial. The analogous question for Nori/Ayoub motivic Galois groups is subtle but largely understood rationally. The integral and relative-to-X version is less commonly stated, though not clearly new.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard spreading-out plus topological-path argument in the Tannakian setting. The alpha-by-alpha versus global distinction is a nice subtlety, but the result is folklore and close to known statements (Deligne, Serre conjugate varieties).
transcription_corrections: 'pas k est alg. clos dans k(X)' should probably read 'par là/donc k est alg. clos dans k(X)'.
The reduction step reads roughly 'on a ainsi k = k_0 (algébriquement clos), où on obtient le résultat voulu grâce au groupe fondamental transcendant'. 'k = E [?] (k_0)' is a misreading.
The marginal diagrams show X_0 → X over A_0 → k and E → A_0, i.e. the spreading-out square.
